slot.brief: Ask about inversion/retention and racemisation for a chiral substrate under SN1 vs SN2 conditions, or which substrate/conditions lead to racemisation.

stem: Optically pure $(S)$-3-bromo-3-methylhexane is subjected to hydrolysis in aqueous acetone. The substitution product obtained is:
options: optically active due to complete inversion
optically active due to complete retention
optically inactive due to the formation of a meso compound

verdicts.working: C3 bears Br, CH3, C2H5, C3H7 — a tertiary stereocenter. Hydrolysis in aqueous acetone (weak nucleophile, ionizing solvent) proceeds by SN1 via a planar tertiary carbocation; water attacks both faces equally, giving racemic 3-methylhexan-3-ol. The product has one stereocenter with four different groups, so it cannot be meso.

working:
1. Identify the substrate structure: 3-bromo-3-methylhexane has four different groups attached to carbon-3 ($-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{Br}$), making it a chiral tertiary alkyl halide.
2. Determine the mechanism: Because the substrate is tertiary and the nucleophile/solvent is weakly nucleophilic and polar protic (water in aqueous acetone), the reaction proceeds exclusively via the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway.
3. Stereochemical outcome: The rate-determining step involves the loss of $\text{Br}^-$ to generate an achiral, planar $sp^2$-hybridised tertiary carbocation: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
Nucleophilic attack of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ occurs with equal probability from either the top or bottom face of this planar intermediate. Deprotonation then yields an equimolar (50:50) mixture of $(R)$- and $(S)$-3-methylhexan-3-ol.
4. Optical activity: This 1:1 enantiomeric pair forms a racemic mixture, which is optically inactive by external compensation (racemisation).

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A assumes an SN2 mechanism with Walden inversion, failing to recognize that tertiary halides do not undergo SN2 substitution due to steric hindrance.
Option B assumes retention of configuration (such as in an SNi pathway), which does not occur under standard aqueous solvolysis.
Option D incorrectly attributes the optical inactivity to internal compensation (a meso compound), which is impossible because the product contains only one stereocenter.
